subject: ACME - Integration follow-up: SDK auth, RSP schema, chat vs completions

Hi Alex - great call this morning, thanks for the time. Recap + next steps below so we have a single place to track action items.

Summary from today
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood for customer-facing NLU features (chat + structured output for support flows) and a reranker pipeline for search results.
- Constraints: front-end expects streaming partial outputs, backend wants deterministic structured JSON for downstream parsers, internal security team requires API-key-based auth with optional mTLS later, token budget target ~1.2k tokens / request average.

Open/confirm items for your team
1) Auth: Are you planning to use a service account pattern (server-to-server with API key) or user-scoped OAuth for calls originating from the browser? We recommend server-side proxy for keys.
2) Response schema: please share a representative request/response example for your support flow (intent, entities, suggested next actions). Attached is a sample RSP schema we often use - can you attach one from your side?
3) Streaming: you mentioned needing partial tokens for UX. Do you need token-level updates (every chunk) or stanza-level (sentence/paragraph)?
4) Embeddings/rerank: confirm vector DB (you mentioned Pinecone) and whether you prefer on-the-fly reranking or precompute embeddings + offline scoring.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf, rsp-schema-examples.md

Proposed next steps
- You: send sample RSP payload + confirm auth approach (by EOD Thu).
- Us: provide SDK snippet and mapping notes for chat vs completions, recommended stop sequences, and streaming semantics (by Fri).
- Sync: 30m technical follow-up next week to walk the SDK snippet and auth flow.

Thanks - I'll loop in Dev on the SDK bits and Dylan will lead the routing/ops discussion.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ACME - Integration follow-up & RSP schema questions

Thanks Marissa - great summary. Quick answers and some follow-ups from our side: 

Auth
- We will be using a server-side service account that our API gateway holds. No browser keys. We can start with API keys and move to mTLS for production.

Response schema
- Attaching a representative payload (acme-rsp-sample-payload.json). Our current pipeline expects: {"intent":string, "entities":[], "actions":[] } and we need a deterministic JSON object (no free-text wrapper).

Chat vs completions + streaming
- Our frontend consumes streaming partial responses to render an assistant UI; token-level streaming preferred but stanza-level is acceptable if it reduces reordering.
- We use server-side post-processing to detect end-of-turn via explicit stop tokens or end-of-stream.

Embeddings/rerank
- We use Pinecone and typically compute embeddings for each chunk on ingest, then do a kNN + rerank pass at query time. We'd like to try on-the-fly reranking if it helps freshness.

Questions for you
1) For structured outputs, is there a recommended best-practice for enforcement (schema validation vs model-constrained output like tool-calling)?
2) How does Redwood count tokens for stop sequences and structured output wrappers?
3) Max tokens: we are often hitting ~4096 tokens in a worst-case search + context scenario - what limits should we expect and how do you suggest truncation strategies?

Thanks - attaching the sample payload. Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up next Tue/Wed.

--Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Acme, Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Integration follow-up & RSP schema questions

Thanks Alex - great context and useful sample. Below are concrete recommendations mapped to your questions. I tried to keep this prescriptive so your engineers can move quickly.

1) Enforcing structured outputs
- Recommended: use model tool-calling (structured output / JSON schema) to explicitly ask the model to return a JSON object. This gives higher reliability than free-text + post-hoc parsing.
- Add a lightweight schema validator on your side (JSON Schema) as a safety net for unexpected tokens. If the model fails validation, fall back to a constrained completions call (or retry with a stricter prompt).

2) Token counting & stop sequences
- Tokenization: Redwood uses standard BPE tokenization for the model family. Token accounting includes prompt tokens + response tokens + stop tokens when they are returned by the model. If you include stop sequences in the request, tokens consumed up to the stop event are billed.
- Stop sequences: prefer explicit string tokens if you can (e.g., "<END_RESPONSE>") - these are reliable. For streaming, the stop is signaled on the server side and the stream closes; you should treat the final event as the canonical end.

3) Max tokens & truncation strategies
- Many Redwood-verified models support 8k or 16k contexts depending on the variant. If you're at ~4096 now, you likely have headroom; we recommend picking a model variant that supports at least 2x your worst case for breathing room.
- Truncation strategy: prioritize recent conversation + documents; for search context, compress long docs into embeddings and pass top-k snippets. Also consider prefix caching for repeated prompts to save tokens.

4) Chat vs completions mapping
- Chat API = structured message list (role + content) - best for multi-turn state and assistant-style prompts.
- Completions = single prompt -> text completion - simpler, sometimes slightly cheaper for one-off responses. For structured JSON output, both can work but chat + function/tool calling is the recommended path for multi-turn assistant flows.

5) Streaming semantics
- Redwood SDK streams delta events with these fields: event_type (partial, final, stop), token, and optional chunk_id for reordering resilience.
- If you need token-level interactivity, render as tokens arrive. If you prefer fewer updates, buffer until punctuation or newline tokens. The SDK supports both via a client-side configuration flag (emit_token_events: true/false).

6) Embeddings & rerankers
- Given you compute embeddings on ingest: keep that and try a hybrid on-the-fly rerank for freshness on top-k results. Redwood suggests re-scoring the top 150 candidates with a light cross-encoder (or a cheaper relevance model) to reduce latency.

Sample SDK snippet (high level)
- Auth: use server-side API key stored in vault, call Redwood.chat.create with messages + function schema for structured output. Include streaming: true for partial updates.
- Example stop: ["<END_RESPONSE>"] and max_tokens set to (model_limit - estimated_prompt_tokens).

- Integration drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-integration

Let me know if you want this as a short demo next Tue (I can share my screen and walk through the SDK).

Best,
Marissa
